sections.title: Letter sound ele
paragraphs: The letter (ele) /ˈele/ makes a clear sound in Spanish. You hear it in (luna) /ˈlu.na/, which means moon. This letter has three sounds, depending on the letter that follows it.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Put the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Let the air flow past the sides of your tongue. Turn your voice on. For the next sound, touch your upper teeth directly with your tongue tip. For the last sound, raise the middle of your tongue toward the hard roof of your mouth. Touch your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: You use the standard sound in most words, like (sol) /sol/. Before the letters t or d, your tongue touches the upper teeth, as in (alto) /ˈal̪.to/. When the next sound is palatal, the middle of your tongue lifts, as in (el chico) /elʲ ˈt͡ʃi.ko/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make a dark sound at the end of a syllable, like the l in ball. Keep the back of your tongue down and keep the sound bright, as in leaf.
